D015-D007_h001.question:
"It's been over a year now, more like thirteen, fourteen months, since this dark cloud settled over me. I just feel so… heavy. Getting out of bed for work at the toll booth feels like lifting a truck, and once I’m there, I just go through the motions. All the joy from the little things in life, gone. My mind feels like it's constantly slogging through mud; I can't think straight or focus on anything. Most days, I just want it all to end. I’ve pictured it, you know, just driving right off the bridge on my way home, or maybe just not waking up.

And then there are these… moments. I hear voices sometimes, whispering my name, or telling me I'm special, destined for something great, chosen for some important task. It’s hard to explain, but it feels so real, like those voices are imparting some profound truth about my hidden power. But these things only happen when I’m really deep in this slump, you know, when I feel the lowest. Once I feel even a tiny bit better, the voices and these thoughts about being special, they just, poof, disappear."
D015-D007_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D015-D007_h001.answer: D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h002.question:
"I'm not exactly sure where to start. It's been over a year now, about thirteen months, that I've been feeling... well, not myself. It's like a dull ache, but not physical. It's like I'm watching my own life from behind a foggy pane of glass. My thoughts get so muddled sometimes, it's hard to focus on anything.

And then there are these other things that have started happening, only when I'm feeling this low. Lately, I'm convinced something's seriously wrong with my insides, like my organs are failing. It's this deep certainty, even though all the doctors say I'm perfectly healthy. Sometimes, I swear I can feel bugs crawling on my skin, even when I'm alone in a room, and I know there's nothing there. It's terrifying. These feelings, the crawling and the thoughts about my body, they only ever happen when I'm really down like this, never when I feel a bit more normal. I’ve even had these sudden, overwhelming urges to just run out into traffic, or jump from the balcony of our penthouse. It’s not that I want to, but the impulse is just… there."
D015-D007_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D015-D007_h002.answer: D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D007_h004.question:
